sources_summary: 100% regional/national & scholarly archaeological registers (UCL CAAL 22,454, Uzbekistan Cabinet Res. 846 6,156, Published Excavations Atlas 2,642, POLARIS IA RAS frontier 2,384, ArchAtlas 2,317, Pleiades 1,613, c14/p3k14c/NERD 1,346, AADR v66 885, Al-Thurayya 827, JADE Xinjiang frontier 656, Kazakhstan Adilet Order 88 185); 0% OSM, 0% Wikidata.

inspected_sheets.cartographic_notes: Mid-period Kushan/Kangju/Wusun kriged surface and 1000 AD benchmark align sharply with Ferghana, Zarafshan, Tashkent, Amu Darya, Murghab, Kopet Dag, Syr Darya, and Chu-Talas oasis corridors across all 723 catchments; zero OSM/Wikidata distortion, zero Voronoi blobs, zero modern border cliffs.

Late-period Mongol/Chagatai/Timurid kriged surface and 900 AD benchmark cleanly resolve the Samarkand-Bukhara, Khwarazm, Merv, Ferghana, Otrar-Sauran, and Zhetysu fluvial ribbons while suppressing arid Kyzylkum/Karakum/Ustyurt interiors; gradient panel confirms sharp topographic detail without artificial border steps.

All 9 SARAY chronological horizons from Epipalaeolithic/Neolithic (Jeitun, Kelteminar) through BMAC/Andronovo, Saka/Kushan, Sogdian/Samanid, Timurid, and Khanates display coherent fluvial oasis concentration and smooth steppe gradients without Voronoi halos or artificial state-border walls.

Unmasked northern Kazakh steppe frontier mosaic (43,5-56,5 N) across 2000 BC, 1 AD, 1000 AD, 1200 AD, 1500 AD, 1700 AD, and 1900 AD confirms continuous cross-border density blending between SARAY and POLARIS with zero step discontinuity along the Russia-Kazakhstan border.

Velkscala reconciled total and rural surfaces (2000 BC, 1200 AD, 1900 AD, 2025 AD) cleanly align urban and oasis density peaks with Ferghana, Zarafshan, Tashkent, Amu Darya, Syr Darya, and Zhetysu corridors while preserving arid desert baselines and continuous cross-frontier transitions.
